summary: A seated hold with your back against a wall that builds endurance in the quadriceps and glutes.
steps: Stand with your back flat against a wall and your feet about hip-width apart.
Walk your feet forward as you slide down the wall.
Stop when your thighs are parallel to the floor and your knees are bent about 90 degrees.
Stack your knees over your ankles and keep your whole back on the wall.
Hold the position, breathing steadily.
mistakes: Knees drifting in front of the toes

summary: A step forward into a split stance that strengthens the quadriceps, glutes, and hamstrings one leg at a time.
steps: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart.
Take a long step forward with one leg.
Lower your hips until both knees are bent about 90 degrees and the back knee is just above the floor.
Push through the front foot to step back to standing.
Switch sides.
cues: Front knee tracks over the toes

summary: A step backward into a lunge that strengthens the glutes, hamstrings, and quadriceps with an easy-to-control landing.
steps: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart.
Step one foot back and land on the ball of that foot.
Lower until both knees are bent about 90 degrees, back knee just above the floor.
Drive through the front foot to bring the back leg forward to standing.
Switch sides.
mistakes: Back knee slamming into the floor

summary: A lunge that crosses one leg diagonally behind the other, training the glutes, quadriceps, and inner thighs.
steps: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart.
Step one foot diagonally behind and across the other, as in a curtsy.
Bend both knees and lower until the front thigh is close to parallel with the floor.
Push through the front foot to return to standing.
Switch sides.
mistakes: Twisting the hips toward the back leg
Crossing too far and losing balance

summary: A wide side step into a one-leg squat that strengthens the quadriceps, glutes, and inner thighs.
steps: Stand tall with your feet together.
Take a wide step to one side, keeping both feet pointing forward.
Sit your hips back and bend the stepping knee while the other leg stays straight.
Push off the bent leg to return to the start.
Switch sides.
mistakes: Heel of the working foot lifting
Rounding the back to reach lower

summary: A kneeling forward lean lowered under control that builds strong eccentric hamstring strength.
steps: Kneel on a pad with your ankles anchored under something stable or held by a partner.
Keep your body straight from knees to head with your hips extended.
Lean forward slowly, resisting with your hamstrings for as long as you can.
Catch yourself with your hands when you can no longer control the descent.
Push lightly off the floor and curl back up to kneeling.
mistakes: Bending at the hips to shorten the lever
Dropping fast once the lean starts

summary: A bridge with heels on sliders that curls the legs in and out to strengthen the hamstrings and glutes.
steps: Lie on your back with knees bent and heels on sliders or a towel on a smooth floor.
Lift your hips into a bridge so your body forms a line from shoulders to knees.
Slowly slide your heels away until your legs are nearly straight, keeping hips up.
Pull your heels back toward your hips, staying in the bridge.
Lower your hips to the floor when the set is finished.
mistakes: Hips dropping as the legs extend

summary: A one-leg hip hinge that strengthens the hamstrings, glutes, and lower back while challenging balance.
steps: Stand on one leg with a soft bend in the knee.
Hinge at the hips, lowering your torso as the free leg extends straight behind you.
Keep your back flat and your hips square to the floor.
Lower until you feel a stretch in the standing hamstring.
Squeeze the glute to return to standing, then switch sides.
cues: Long line from head to heel
mistakes: Opening the hip of the raised leg
Bending the standing knee into a squat

summary: A hip lift from the floor that strengthens the glutes and hamstrings and teaches full hip extension.
steps: Lie on your back with knees bent, feet flat and hip-width apart, arms by your sides.
Brace your core and press through your heels.
Lift your hips until your body forms a straight line from shoulders to knees.
Squeeze your glutes and pause briefly at the top.
Lower your hips slowly to the floor.
cues: Squeeze the glutes at the top
mistakes: Arching the lower back instead of extending the hips

summary: A hip extension with the shoulders on a bench that strongly loads the glutes and hamstrings.
steps: Sit with your upper back against the edge of a bench, knees bent and feet flat.
Brace your core and tuck your chin slightly.
Drive through your heels to lift your hips until your torso and thighs are level.
Squeeze your glutes hard at the top with shins roughly vertical.
Lower your hips under control.
mistakes: Arching the lower back at the top
Feet too far out, shifting work to hamstrings

summary: A hands-and-knees kick that lifts one bent leg toward the ceiling to isolate and strengthen the glutes.
steps: Start on hands and knees with hands under shoulders and knees under hips.
Keep one knee bent 90 degrees and lift that leg back and up, sole toward the ceiling.
Squeeze the glute at the top without arching your lower back.
Lower the knee back under the hip with control.
Switch sides.
mistakes: Arching the lower back to lift higher

summary: A step onto a raised surface that builds single-leg strength in the quadriceps and glutes.
steps: Stand facing a sturdy box, bench, or step.
Place one whole foot on top of the surface.
Drive through that foot to stand up tall on the box.
Step down slowly with the same leg you lifted last.
Switch sides.
mistakes: Knee caving inward on the way up

summary: A step-up finished with a strong knee drive that builds single-leg power for running and jumping.
steps: Stand facing a sturdy box or bench.
Place one whole foot on top of the box.
Drive through that foot to stand up tall.
As you rise, drive the other knee up to hip height, sprinter style.
Step back down with control and switch sides.
mistakes: Leaning back during the knee drive

summary: A slow single-leg lowering off a step that strengthens the quadriceps and glutes with knee control.
steps: Stand on one leg on a step with the other foot hanging off the edge.
Bend the standing knee and sit your hips back slightly.
Lower slowly until the free heel lightly touches the floor below.
Push through the standing foot to return to the top.
Switch sides.
mistakes: Hip of the free leg sagging

summary: A calf raise on one foot that strengthens the calves and ankle with twice the load of a two-foot raise.
steps: Stand on one foot, lightly holding a wall or support for balance.
Rise onto the ball of the foot as high as you can.
Pause briefly at the top.
Lower your heel slowly to the floor.
Switch sides.
cues: Rise as high as you can
mistakes: Using the hand to push up

summary: A lift of the toes toward the shins that strengthens the muscles at the front of the lower leg.
steps: Lean your back against a wall with your feet a short step in front of you.
Keep your legs straight and your heels on the floor.
Lift your toes and the balls of your feet as high as you can.
Lower your toes slowly back to the floor.
cues: Pull the toes to the shins

summary: A squat followed by a vertical jump that builds lower-body power in the quadriceps, glutes, and calves.
steps: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and chest up.
Squat down until your thighs are near parallel.
Swing your arms and jump straight up as high as you can.
Land softly on the balls of your feet and sink back into the squat.
mistakes: Rounding the back at the bottom

summary: A two-foot jump onto a raised platform that develops explosive power in the legs and hips.
steps: Stand a short step from a stable box with feet hip-width apart.
Dip into a quarter squat and swing your arms back.
Swing your arms forward and jump onto the box.
Land softly with both feet flat, knees bent, then stand tall.
Step back down one foot at a time.
mistakes: Jumping down instead of stepping down
Landing on the edge of the box

summary: A jumping lunge that switches legs in the air, building leg power and coordination.
steps: Start in a lunge with one foot forward and the back knee just above the floor.
Jump up explosively, swinging your arms for height.
Switch your legs in the air.
Land softly in a lunge with the other foot forward and flow into the next jump.

summary: A forward jump from a deep squat that builds explosive power in the quadriceps, glutes, and calves.
steps: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and squat down with chest up.
Swing your arms and jump forward as far as you can.
Land softly back into the squat, absorbing the impact through your legs.
Reset your position before the next jump.
mistakes: Rounding the back at the bottom

summary: A side-to-side single-leg bound that builds lateral power and stability in the glutes and legs.
steps: Stand on one leg in a half squat.
Push off hard and leap sideways onto the opposite foot.
Land softly in a half squat, letting the free leg swing behind you.
Stick the landing briefly, then bound back to the other side.
mistakes: Landing upright with a stiff leg

summary: A static plank on the forearms and toes that trains the core to keep the body straight.
steps: Place your forearms on the floor with elbows under your shoulders.
Step your feet back so you rest on your toes.
Squeeze your glutes and brace your abs so your body forms a line from head to heels.
Hold the position, breathing steadily.

summary: A sideways hold on one forearm that strengthens the obliques and stabilizes the spine.
steps: Lie on your side with your elbow under your shoulder and legs stacked.
Lift your hips so your body forms a line from head to feet.
Keep your hips stacked and pressed forward.
Hold the position, breathing steadily.
Switch sides.

summary: A side plank with slow thread-the-needle reaches that trains the obliques and shoulder stability.
steps: Set up in a side plank on your forearm with feet stacked and hips lifted.
Reach your top arm toward the ceiling.
Slowly rotate your torso and thread the top arm under your body.
Rotate back open to the ceiling while your hips stay high.
Keep holding and rotating, breathing steadily, then switch sides.

summary: A hold lying on your back with arms and legs lifted that teaches full-body tension through the abs.
steps: Lie on your back with arms overhead and legs straight.
Press your lower back firmly into the floor.
Lift your shoulders, arms, and legs a few inches off the floor.
Point your toes and keep your arms by your ears.
Hold the position, breathing steadily.
mistakes: Lower back arching off the floor

summary: A rocking movement in the hollow body position that trains the abs to keep full-body tension.
steps: Lie on your back and lift into a hollow hold with arms overhead and legs straight.
Keep your lower back pressed down and your body in a shallow banana shape.
Rock back toward your shoulders and forward toward your hips.
Keep the shape rigid so the whole body moves as one piece.
cues: Rock from the hips, not the arms
mistakes: Bending at the hips to create the rock
Arms swinging to drive the motion

summary: A slow alternating limb reach lying on your back that trains the core to stay still against movement.
steps: Lie on your back with arms reaching to the ceiling and hips and knees bent 90 degrees.
Exhale and press your lower back into the floor.
Slowly extend one leg and the opposite arm toward the floor without touching it.
Return to the start and repeat on the other side.
mistakes: Lower back arching off the floor
Moving the same-side arm and leg

summary: A support hold on the hands with straight legs held level, building core compression and arm strength.
steps: Sit with legs straight together and hands flat beside your hips.
Lock your elbows and press down to lift your hips off the floor.
Lift your straight legs until they are parallel to the floor.
Push your shoulders down away from your ears.
Hold the position, breathing steadily.

summary: A support hold on the hands with straight legs raised above horizontal, demanding strong compression.
steps: Start in an L-sit with hands beside your hips and legs straight.
Press tall through your arms and lean your shoulders slightly back.
Pull your straight legs higher so they rise above horizontal into a V shape.
Keep your shoulders depressed and your knees locked.
Hold the position, breathing steadily.
cues: Pull the legs to the chest
mistakes: Knees bending to raise the legs

summary: An elite support hold with legs lifted past vertical behind the hands, requiring extreme compression.
steps: Start in a high V-sit on the floor or parallettes with fingers pointing back.
Lean your shoulders back behind your hands and press firmly into the floor.
Pull your hips forward and lift your straight legs toward your face.
Keep pressing until your legs pass vertical and your hips rise.
Hold the position, breathing steadily.
cues: Pull the legs to the face

summary: A straight-body lever lowered from the shoulders on a bench that builds elite abdominal strength.
steps: Lie on a bench and grip the bench or a post firmly behind your head.
Roll your body up onto your upper back until it is nearly vertical.
Keep a straight line from shoulders to toes with hips extended.
Lower your body slowly as one rigid unit until it hovers above the bench.
Raise back up without bending at the hips.

summary: A knee raise from a dead hang that strengthens the abdominals and hip flexors without swinging.
steps: Hang from a bar with arms straight and shoulders engaged.
Brace your core to stop any swing.
Raise your knees toward your chest, curling your pelvis up at the top.
Lower your legs slowly to the hang.
mistakes: Using momentum to swing the legs

summary: A straight-leg raise from a dead hang that builds strong abdominals, hip flexors, and grip.
steps: Hang from a bar with arms straight and legs together.
Brace your core and tilt your pelvis slightly back.
Raise your straight legs to horizontal or higher.
Pause briefly at the top.
Lower your legs slowly to the hang without swinging.

summary: An advanced hanging core move that swings straight legs side to side above the bar, training the obliques, abs and grip.
steps: Hang from a pull-up bar with an overhand grip and your shoulders actively pulled down.
Raise your straight legs until your feet are near the bar, keeping them together.
Rotate your legs slowly to one side like a wiper, keeping your hips high.
Sweep them through the center and over to the other side under control.
Return to center and lower your legs slowly to finish.
mistakes: Dropping the hips during the rotation
Bending the knees to shorten the lever

summary: An elite sideways hold on a vertical pole that demands full-body strength through the core, lats, and shoulders.
steps: Grip a vertical pole with hands wider than shoulders, top hand overhand and bottom hand underhand.
Lock both arms straight, pulling with the top arm and pushing with the bottom arm.
Jump or kick your legs up to the side.
Squeeze your body into a straight line level with the floor.
Hold the position, breathing steadily.

summary: A forward roll on an ab wheel that strengthens the core against spinal extension, with lats and shoulders.
steps: Kneel on a pad and hold an ab wheel under your shoulders.
Brace your core and tuck your pelvis slightly.
Roll the wheel forward slowly, extending your body as far as you can control.
Pull the wheel back toward your knees using your abs and lats.
mistakes: Lower back sagging at full extension
Leading the return with the hips
Rolling farther than you can control

summary: A seated torso rotation side to side that strengthens the obliques and abdominals.
steps: Sit with knees bent and lean back so your torso forms a V with your thighs.
Lift your feet off the floor, or keep heels down for an easier version.
Clasp your hands in front of your chest.
Rotate your torso to one side, then through the center to the other side.

summary: An alternating elbow-to-knee crunch in a pedaling motion that works the abdominals and obliques.
steps: Lie on your back with hands lightly behind your head and legs lifted.
Lift your shoulders off the floor.
Bring one knee toward your chest while rotating the opposite elbow toward it.
Extend that leg as you switch sides in a smooth pedaling motion.
mistakes: Moving only the elbows, not the torso

summary: An opposite arm and leg reach from all fours that builds core and glute stability with a neutral spine.
steps: Start on hands and knees with hands under shoulders and knees under hips.
Brace your core and keep your spine neutral.
Extend one arm forward and the opposite leg back until both are level with your torso.
Pause briefly, then return to the start without losing position.
Repeat on the other side.

summary: A face-down hold with arms and legs lifted that strengthens the glutes, back, and shoulders.
steps: Lie face down with arms extended overhead and legs straight.
Squeeze your glutes and brace your core.
Lift your arms, chest, and legs a few inches off the floor.
Keep your neck long with your gaze toward the floor.
Hold the position, breathing steadily.

summary: A face-down arched hold, the counterpart to the hollow hold, that trains the glutes, back, and shoulders.
steps: Lie face down with arms overhead and legs together.
Squeeze your glutes and pull your shoulder blades back and down.
Lift your arms, chest, and legs into a smooth, even arch.
Keep your arms by your ears and your neck in line with your spine.
Hold the position, breathing steadily.
mistakes: Bending only at the lower back

summary: A lying knee pull that curls the hips off the floor to strengthen the lower abdominals.
steps: Lie on your back with arms by your sides and palms down.
Lift your legs so your thighs are vertical and knees bent.
Curl your pelvis up, lifting your hips off the floor as your knees move toward your chest.
Lower your hips slowly back to the floor.

summary: A lying jackknife that lifts straight legs and torso together to strengthen the abdominals.
steps: Lie on your back with arms overhead and legs straight.
Brace your core and lift your arms and legs together.
Reach your hands toward your toes, balancing on your hips at the top.
Lower your arms and legs slowly back toward the floor.

summary: A fast alternating knee drive from a high plank that raises the heart rate and trains the core.
steps: Start in a high plank with hands under shoulders and body straight.
Drive one knee toward your chest.
Switch legs quickly, extending the bent leg as the other knee drives in.
Keep alternating at a steady pace with your hips level.

summary: A lying straight-leg raise that strengthens the abdominals and hip flexors.
steps: Lie on your back with legs straight and hands by your sides or under your hips.
Press your lower back into the floor.
Raise your straight legs until they point at the ceiling.
Lower them slowly, stopping before your lower back lifts.
mistakes: Lower back arching as the legs lower

summary: A seated active lift of straight legs that builds hip-flexor strength and compression for L-sits.
steps: Sit tall with legs straight together and hands on the floor beside your knees.
Lean forward slightly and fold your chest toward your thighs.
Lift both straight legs off the floor using only your hip flexors and abs.
Lower your legs slowly.
mistakes: Leaning back to lift the legs

summary: A high plank held while tapping alternate shoulders, training the core to resist rotation.
steps: Start in a high plank with hands under shoulders and feet a bit wider than hip-width.
Brace your core and squeeze your glutes.
Lift one hand and tap the opposite shoulder, then return it.
Alternate hands while keeping your hips still, breathing steadily.

summary: A forearm plank rocked forward and back that loads the core and shoulders through a longer lever.
steps: Set up in a forearm plank with feet on sliders or a smooth floor.
Brace your core and squeeze your glutes.
Push your body back by moving at the shoulders so your elbows go past your head.
Pull back to the plank position, keeping your body straight.
mistakes: Lower back sagging as you push back
Moving farther than you can control

summary: A freestanding balance upside down on the hands that builds shoulder, arm, and wrist strength.
steps: Place your hands shoulder-width apart on the floor with fingers spread.
Kick up with one leg and bring the other to meet it overhead.
Stack your body vertically over your hands with arms locked.
Balance by pressing through your fingers and palms.
Hold the position, breathing steadily, then step down.
mistakes: Kicking up too hard and overbalancing

summary: A slow lift into a handstand from the floor without a kick, requiring elite strength and flexibility.
steps: Stand with feet together and place your hands on the floor in front of your feet.
Shift your shoulders forward over your hands until your feet become light.
Lift your hips over your shoulders, keeping your arms straight.
Raise your legs slowly to vertical without kicking or jumping.
Hold the handstand briefly, then lower with control.

summary: A horizontal balance on bent arms with the elbows in the hips, building wrist, forearm, and shoulder control.
steps: Squat down and place your hands on the floor with fingers pointing back or to the sides.
Bend your elbows and press them into your hips or lower abdomen.
Lean forward until your feet lift off the floor.
Extend your legs straight back so your body is level with the floor.
Hold the position, breathing steadily.
mistakes: Leaning too far and tipping onto the face

summary: An arm balance with the knees on the backs of the upper arms that builds shoulder and wrist strength.
steps: Squat down and place your hands on the floor shoulder-width apart, fingers spread.
Bend your elbows slightly and place your knees high on the backs of your upper arms.
Shift your weight forward onto your hands until your feet lift off the floor.
Look slightly ahead and keep your hips high.
Hold the position, breathing steadily.
mistakes: Dropping the head and tipping forward

summary: An elite rings hold with arms straight out to the sides that demands extreme chest, biceps, and shoulder strength.
steps: Start in a support or hang on the rings with arms straight.
Turn the rings slightly out and lock your elbows.
Spread your arms out to the sides slowly until they are level with your shoulders.
Keep your body vertical with legs together.
Hold the position, breathing steadily.

summary: An elite horizontal hold on rings with arms out to the sides, body parallel to the floor, face down.
steps: Start in a planche position on the rings with arms straight.
Spread your arms out to the sides while lowering your body toward horizontal.
Keep your hands near hip level and your elbows locked.
Hold your body straight and parallel to the floor.
Hold the position, breathing steadily.

summary: An elite face-up horizontal hold on rings with arms out to the sides, built on lat and shoulder strength.
steps: Start in a back lever on the rings with arms straight.
Spread your arms out wide to the sides.
Keep your body straight and level, chest facing up.
Pull down hard through straight arms to hold your height.
Hold the position, breathing steadily.

summary: A locked-arm support at the top of a dip on rings that builds chest, triceps, and shoulder stability.
steps: Grip the rings and jump up to support yourself with arms straight.
Keep the rings close to your hips and lock your elbows.
Turn the rings slightly out, thumbs pointing away.
Push your shoulders down and keep your body straight.
Hold the position, breathing steadily.
mistakes: Rings drifting away from the body

summary: A full backbend on hands and feet that builds glute, shoulder, and spinal extension strength and flexibility.
steps: Lie on your back with knees bent, feet flat, and hands beside your ears, fingers toward your feet.
Press through your feet to lift your hips.
Press through your hands to lift your head and straighten your arms.
Push your chest toward the wall behind you with arms locked.
Hold the position, breathing steadily, then lower slowly.
mistakes: Bent arms leaving weight on the head

summary: An arched bridge on the head and feet that strengthens the neck and back extensors.
steps: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat, close to your hips.
Place your hands beside your head for support.
Lift your hips and roll back onto the top of your head.
Keep your hands ready to take weight, moving only through a comfortable range.
Hold the position, breathing steadily, then lower slowly.
mistakes: Taking all weight on the neck at once
Feet too far from the hips

summary: An elite handstand on rings with a deep forward lean and hands near the hips, demanding huge shoulder strength.
steps: Press into a handstand on the rings with arms straight.
Turn the rings out and keep them close to your body.
Lean your shoulders forward while lowering your hands toward hip level.
Keep your body straight and your elbows locked.
Hold the position, breathing steadily.
mistakes: Rings drifting away from the body

summary: A straight-arm press from a planche up into a handstand that demands elite shoulder and chest strength.
steps: Start in a planche with arms straight and body level.
Lean your shoulders forward and begin lifting your hips.
Keep your arms locked as your legs rise toward vertical.
Finish stacked in a handstand.
Hold briefly, then lower with control.

summary: An elite handstand push-up that lowers onto the forearms and presses back up, built on triceps and shoulder strength.
steps: Kick up into a handstand, against a wall if needed.
Lower one forearm and then the other to the floor, or both together under control.
Balance briefly in a forearm stand.
Press through your hands to straighten your arms back to a handstand.
mistakes: Arching the lower back on the press

summary: A full-body squat, plank, push-up, and jump sequence that builds conditioning and strength.
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Squat down and place your hands on the floor in front of your feet.
Jump your feet back into a high plank and do a push-up.
Jump your feet back toward your hands.
Jump up with arms overhead and land softly.
mistakes: Lower back sagging in the plank

summary: A burpee followed by a jump to a bar and a pull-up, combining conditioning with back strength.
steps: Stand under a bar you can reach with a small jump.
Squat, jump your feet back to a plank, do a push-up, and jump your feet in.
Jump up and grab the bar with both hands.
Pull until your chin is above the bar.
Lower under control and drop down softly.
mistakes: Missing the grip on the jump

summary: A step off a box into an immediate rebound jump that trains reactive power in the legs.
steps: Stand on a low, stable box.
Step off the box, do not jump, and land on both feet.
Spend as little time on the ground as possible.
Rebound straight up into a maximal jump.
Land softly with knees bent.
mistakes: Box too high to rebound quickly
Sinking deep on the first landing

summary: A crawl on hands and feet with knees hovering that builds shoulder, core, and leg endurance.
steps: Start on hands and knees, then lift your knees an inch off the floor.
Keep your back flat and your hips level with your shoulders.
Move one hand and the opposite foot forward a short step.
Repeat with the other hand and foot, keeping knees low.

summary: A face-up walk on hands and feet that strengthens the triceps, glutes, and hamstrings.
steps: Sit with knees bent, feet flat, and hands behind you with fingers pointing toward your feet.
Lift your hips off the floor into a tabletop position.
Walk forward, backward, or sideways by moving opposite hand and foot together.
Keep your hips up throughout.

summary: A crawling transition that threads one leg under the body to a seated reach, training core and shoulders.
steps: Start on hands and feet with knees hovering just above the floor.
Lift one hand and rotate your hips toward that side.
Kick the opposite leg through under your body until it is straight.
Return the leg and hand to the start and repeat on the other side.

summary: An explosive push-up that launches the body into a pike in the air, building chest and triceps power.
steps: Start in a high plank with hands under shoulders.
Lower your chest toward the floor.
Push explosively so your hands and feet leave the floor.
Pike your hips up and touch your toes in the air.
Land softly back in the plank with elbows bent.
mistakes: Not getting enough height to pike

summary: An explosive dip that drives the hands off the bars, building elite triceps, chest, and shoulder power.
steps: Support yourself on parallel bars with arms straight.
Lower into a dip until your shoulders are just below your elbows.
Push explosively so your hands leave the bars at the top.
Catch the bars with soft elbows and flow into the next dip.
mistakes: Missing the bars on the catch
Dipping too shallow to generate power

summary: A spring from lying on your back up to your feet that builds hip power, coordination, and timing.
steps: Lie on your back with hands beside your ears, palms down.
Roll back onto your shoulders and bring your knees toward your face.
Kick your legs up and forward explosively while pushing through your hands.
Snap your hips forward and land on your feet in a squat, then stand up.
mistakes: Kicking straight up instead of forward

summary: A swing of the legs up and over a bar to finish in a support, training lats, biceps, and core.
steps: Hang from a low bar with an overhand grip.
Pull your chest toward the bar while driving your legs up.
Bring your hips to the bar and rotate your legs over it.
Finish in a front support on top with arms straight.
Lower back down under control.
cues: Pull the bar to the hips
mistakes: Letting the arms straighten too early

summary: A walk out from standing to a plank and back that stretches the hamstrings and warms up the shoulders.
steps: Stand with feet together.
Hinge forward with legs as straight as is comfortable and place your hands on the floor.
Walk your hands forward until you reach a high plank.
Walk your feet in toward your hands with small steps, keeping legs straight.
Roll up to standing.
mistakes: Lower back sagging in the plank

summary: An explosive jump that spreads the arms and legs into an X shape, building leg power and coordination.
steps: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and arms by your sides.
Squat down halfway.
Jump as high as you can, spreading your arms and legs into an X.
Bring your limbs back in and land softly with knees bent.
mistakes: Holding the X into the landing

summary: An overhead arc with a stick or band from front to back that improves shoulder mobility.
steps: Hold a stick or band in front of your hips with a wide grip.
Keep your arms straight and raise them overhead.
Continue the arc behind you until the stick reaches your lower back.
Reverse the arc slowly to return to the front.
mistakes: Bending the elbows to get through

summary: A slide of the arms up and down a wall that improves shoulder mobility and posture.
steps: Stand with your head, upper back, and hips against a wall, feet a little forward.
Raise your arms into a goalpost shape with elbows bent 90 degrees.
Slide your arms up the wall as far as you can while keeping contact.
Slide them back down to the goalpost position.
mistakes: Lower back arching off the wall
Elbows or wrists leaving the wall

summary: A hang on rings or a bar with arms behind the body that stretches the shoulders into full extension.
steps: Hang from low rings or a bar with feet on the floor for support.
Tuck your legs and rotate backward, passing your legs between your arms.
Lower your legs toward the floor behind you so your arms end up behind your body.
Keep your feet on the floor to control how much weight you take.
Hold the position, breathing steadily, then return the way you came.

summary: An alternating arch and round of the spine on all fours that improves spinal mobility.
steps: Start on hands and knees with hands under shoulders and knees under hips.
Inhale and let your belly drop as you lift your chest and tailbone.
Exhale and round your back toward the ceiling, letting your head drop.
Move slowly between the two positions.
cues: Move one segment at a time

summary: A rotation of the upper back from all fours that improves thoracic spine mobility.
steps: Start on hands and knees with one hand behind your head.
Rotate that elbow down toward the opposite hand.
Rotate up, opening your chest and pointing the elbow toward the ceiling.
Switch sides.
cues: Follow the elbow with your eyes
mistakes: Shifting the hips to fake rotation

summary: A slow segment-by-segment roll down of the spine that improves hamstring and spinal flexibility.
steps: Stand tall on a step or the floor with legs straight.
Tuck your chin to your chest.
Roll your spine down one segment at a time, letting your arms hang.
Go only as far as is comfortable.
Roll back up slowly, stacking one segment at a time.
mistakes: Bending the knees to reach lower

summary: A hold at the bottom of a full squat that improves hip, knee, and ankle mobility.
steps: Stand with feet about shoulder-width apart and toes turned slightly out.
Lower into a squat as deep as is comfortable with heels on the floor.
Keep your chest up, using elbows inside the knees or a support if needed.
Hold the position, breathing steadily.

summary: A seated switch between two 90/90 leg positions that improves hip rotation in both directions.
steps: Sit with one leg bent 90 degrees in front and the other bent 90 degrees to the side.
Sit tall, with hands behind you for support if needed.
Rotate both knees over to the other side so the legs swap positions.
Keep your feet on the floor and move slowly.
mistakes: Lifting the feet off the floor

summary: A floor stretch with the front shin across the body that opens the outer hip and hip flexors.
steps: Start on hands and knees and bring one knee forward behind the same-side wrist.
Angle the front shin across your body.
Slide the back leg straight behind you and lower your hips toward the floor.
Keep your hips square and ease into a pain-free range.
Hold 20–30 seconds, then switch sides.

summary: A wide-knee rock back from all fours that stretches the inner thighs and hips.
steps: Start on hands and knees and widen your knees as far as is comfortable.
Keep your shins parallel and drop down onto your forearms.
Gently rock your hips back toward your heels and then forward.
Stay within a pain-free range.

summary: A kneeling stretch with the back foot up against a wall or couch that opens the quadriceps and hip flexors.
steps: Kneel facing away from a wall or couch with your back shin up against it.
Step the other foot forward into a lunge.
Squeeze the glute of the back leg and lift your torso upright.
Ease your hips forward within a pain-free range, then relax.
Switch sides.

summary: A seated wide-leg forward fold that stretches the inner thighs, hamstrings, and lower back.
steps: Sit with legs straight and spread wide, toes pointing up.
Sit tall and place your hands on the floor in front of you.
Hinge forward from your hips, walking your hands out.
Keep your back long and stay within a pain-free range.
Hold 20–30 seconds, then walk your hands back.

summary: A split stretch with one leg forward and one back that opens the hamstrings and hip flexors.
steps: Start kneeling and extend one leg straight in front of you.
Slide the front heel forward and the back knee back.
Keep your hips square to the front and use your hands for support.
Lower only as far as is comfortable.
Hold 20–30 seconds, then switch sides.

summary: A side split stretch with both legs out wide that opens the inner thighs and hamstrings.
steps: Stand with your feet wide and your hands on your hips.
Slide your feet apart to the sides with toes pointing forward or up.
Lower your hips toward the floor, placing your hands on the floor for support.
Stay within a pain-free range.
Hold 20–30 seconds, then walk your feet back in.
cues: Hips in line with the feet

summary: A face-down press of the chest off the floor that stretches the abdominals and extends the spine.
steps: Lie face down with hands under your shoulders and legs straight.
Press your palms into the floor and lift your chest, keeping your hips down.
Keep your elbows slightly bent and your shoulders away from your ears.
Hold 20–30 seconds, then lower slowly.
cues: Lift only as far as comfortable

summary: A standing knee drive toward a wall that improves ankle mobility for squats and lunges.
steps: Stand facing a wall with one foot a few inches from it.
Keep the heel flat and drive your knee forward toward the wall over your toes.
Return the knee back to the start.
Move your foot back slightly as the knee touches more easily, then switch sides.

summary: A gentle warm-up that rolls the hands in slow circles at the wrists to loosen the wrists and forearms.
steps: Stand or sit tall with your elbows bent and forearms held out in front of you.
Make loose fists, or interlace your fingers with the palms together.
Slowly roll your hands in full circles at the wrists, keeping the forearms still.
After several circles, reverse the direction.

summary: A face-down leg swing across the body that mobilizes the hips, hip flexors, and lower spine.
steps: Lie face down with arms out to the sides, palms down.
Bend one knee and swing that foot up and across toward the opposite hand.
Keep your chest and arms on the floor as much as you can.
Return the leg slowly and switch sides.

summary: A lunge with an elbow drop and an upward reach that mobilizes the hips, hamstrings, and upper back.
steps: Step one foot forward into a deep lunge with the back knee off the floor.
Place the same-side hand on the floor and drop that elbow toward the instep.
Place the elbow-side hand back on the floor and rotate the other arm up toward the ceiling.
Return the hand down and straighten the front leg to stretch the hamstring.
Switch sides.
cues: Follow the hand with your eyes
mistakes: Back knee resting on the floor

summary: A side-lying arm sweep across the body that improves upper-back rotation and chest mobility.
steps: Lie on your side with knees bent 90 degrees and arms together in front of you.
Keep your knees together and on the floor.
Sweep the top arm up and over toward the floor behind you, following it with your eyes.
Return the arm slowly to the start, then switch sides.

summary: A fast run in place driving the knees high that raises the heart rate and works the legs and core.
steps: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart.
Drive one knee up toward hip height.
Switch legs quickly, landing on the balls of your feet.
Pump your arms and keep a steady rhythm until the time is up.
cues: Stay on the balls of the feet

summary: A rhythmic jump that opens and closes the arms and legs to raise the heart rate and warm up the body.
steps: Stand tall with feet together and arms by your sides.
Jump your feet out wide while raising your arms overhead.
Jump your feet back together while lowering your arms.
Keep a steady rhythm until the time is up.

summary: A jumping jack performed in a low squat that builds leg endurance in the quadriceps and glutes.
steps: Stand with feet together and sink into a half squat with hands at your chest.
Jump your feet out wide, staying low.
Jump your feet back together, staying low.
Keep a steady rhythm until the time is up.

summary: A jumping jack with the feet from a high plank that trains the core and raises the heart rate.
steps: Start in a high plank with hands under shoulders and feet together.
Jump your feet out wide.
Jump your feet back together.
Keep your hips level and continue until the time is up.

summary: A quick side-to-side shuffle in an athletic stance that builds leg endurance and lateral movement.
steps: Stand in an athletic stance with feet wider than hips, knees bent, and hips back.
Push off the trailing foot to shuffle sideways.
Bring the feet close without letting them cross.
Shuffle a few steps, then change direction, until the time is up.

summary: A squat-to-plank-and-back movement that builds full-body conditioning without the jump or push-up.
steps: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart.
Squat down and place your hands on the floor in front of your feet.
Jump your feet back to a high plank.
Jump your feet back toward your hands.
Stand tall to finish.
mistakes: Lower back sagging in the plank
Feet landing far from the hands

summary: Rapid small steps in a quarter squat that build foot speed and calf endurance.
steps: Stand in a quarter squat with feet hip-width apart.
Stay on the balls of your feet.
Take tiny, rapid steps in place.
Keep your chest up and continue until the time is up.

summary: Quick two-foot hops side to side that build calf spring, coordination, and leg endurance.
steps: Stand with feet together beside a line on the floor.
Hop sideways over the line, landing on both feet.
Hop back over to the start.
Keep hopping side to side until the time is up.
cues: Hop side to side over a line

summary: A static plank on straight arms that trains the core to resist sagging, with shoulder support.
steps: Place your hands under your shoulders and step your feet back.
Squeeze your glutes and quads so your body forms a line from head to heels.
Push the floor away to spread your shoulder blades.
Hold the position, breathing steadily.

summary: A move between forearm and high plank one arm at a time that trains the core, triceps, and shoulders.
steps: Start in a forearm plank with feet hip-width apart.
Place one hand under your shoulder and press up.
Bring the other hand up so you are in a high plank.
Lower back to the forearms one arm at a time.
Alternate the lead arm.
cues: Forearm to high plank, one arm at a time
mistakes: Hips piking up during the press

summary: A forearm plank that rotates the hips toward the floor side to side to work the obliques and abs.
steps: Start in a forearm plank with feet together.
Rotate your hips to lower one hip toward the floor.
Return to center and rotate to the other side.
Keep your shoulders square throughout.
